summary: Pre-deploy responsive audit for Délices Mikaté Royal at 390x844 (mobile), 768x1024 (tablet) and 1440x900 (desktop). No code changes performed (audit-only). Overall: green on prices, delivery two-tier copy, combos, order-form E2E, and layout. One CRITICAL image bug found (Story.jsx points to a .png that does not exist — served as SPA HTML fallback → broken image). Three MINOR touch-target regressions on mobile (cookie banner buttons 40-42 px, hamburger items 41 px, footer legal links 18 px) below the ≥44 px guideline the review requested.

ui_bugs.issue: Hard-coded src '/products/jus-gingembre-luxe.png' does not exist — actual file on disk & backend refs are 'jus-gingembre-luxe.jpg'. curl returns content-type 'text/html' (SPA fallback), naturalWidth=0. Broken image rendered inside the Notre-Histoire / Story block at 342x420 on mobile and equivalent on desktop.
Accept button height = 40 px, Refuser = 42 px, Personnaliser = 42 px — all below the ≥44 px touch-target the review requested.

All 6 mobile menu links (m-nav-home, m-nav-products, m-nav-delivery, m-nav-story, m-nav-testimonials, m-nav-events) render at 41 px height — below the ≥44 px touch-target the review requested. Navigation itself works (tapping 'Menu' scrolls to #produits).

Each legal link renders at 18 px height (Link's default line-height) — well below the ≥32 px comfortable tap the review requested. Legal links are tappable but density is high on 1-column mobile layout.

issues: Broken gingembre image ruins the Story block visual. Change GINGER_IMG in Story.jsx L6 from 'jus-gingembre-luxe.png' to 'jus-gingembre-luxe.jpg' to fix.

critical_code_review_comments: Story.jsx L6 references '/products/jus-gingembre-luxe.png' but the asset is .jpg — this is the only broken image on the site. Backend catalog uses .jpg correctly; only this hard-coded frontend const is wrong.

OrderForm.jsx L353 already applies `min-h-[44px] md:min-h-0` to the Ajouter chips — good pattern; consider reusing it for the hamburger items and cookie banner action buttons so mobile respects the 44 px touch-target rule.
Delivery.jsx uses lg:grid-cols-2 (breakpoint = 1024 px). At tablet 768–1023 the cards stack vertically. Review allowed either — but if a real 2-col-on-tablet is desired, switch to md:grid-cols-2.

Products.jsx ProductCard uses fixed h-60 image container with object-cover — correct behavior for portrait 1122x1402 juice images (bissap/gingembre) and landscape 1408x768 mikaté images: images are cropped, not squished. No aspect distortion in either case.
Footer.jsx legal links have no explicit tap-target sizing — on mobile (1-col) each link is roughly text-height (~18 px). Suggest adding `py-1.5 block` to hit the 32–44 px comfortable tap zone.
Hero.jsx L34 slide 3 description 'livraison dans plusieurs secteurs' still reads OK with the new two-tier delivery scope; low priority.

Navbar mobile hamburger opens correctly and go(id) navigation works, but the drop-down items are py-2.5 without a min-h floor — they compute to 41 px which is 3 px short of Apple/Material 44 px guideline.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fixes are all localized single-line/attribute changes (Story.jsx image ext, min-h utilities on 3 components). After fixes: (1) reload / at 390x844 and verify jus-gingembre-luxe.jpg loads with naturalWidth=1122 in the Story block, (2) re-measure cookie banner + hamburger + footer legal link heights ≥44 px / ≥32 px. Everything else in the audit (prices, delivery two-tier, combos, order-form E2E, no h-scroll, no forbidden legacy strings, hero captions, image proportions, legal pages) is green and does not need re-test unless a global refactor is made.
rca of the issue: Broken gingembre image: developer copy-pasted the constant during the recent luxe-image rename and left the .png extension while the actual asset was saved as .jpg. Server returns text/html because index.html is served as SPA fallback for unknown paths, which masked the 404 in DevTools Network unless inspecting content-type. Touch-target regressions: Navbar mobile items, cookie banner buttons and footer legal links use small padding without a min-h utility, so at mobile density they slip below the 44 px / 32 px thresholds the review specifically called out.
